title: Verdier axioms and stagewise triangulation
statement:
The shift and distinguished triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]
satisfy the four Verdier axioms:

1. every morphism has a distinguished cone triangle, the identity triangle
   is distinguished, and distinguishedness is closed under isomorphism;
2. a triangle is distinguished if and only if its signed rotation is
   distinguished;
3. every commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
   triangles extends to a morphism of triangles;
4. cone triangles for composable maps can be placed in an octahedral diagram
   whose required faces commute and whose remaining cone triangle is
   distinguished.

Consequently $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated category. Every
finite-stage inclusion $j_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal P_T$ is exact, and
the identifications $j_FT_{F/E}\simeq j_E$ are exact natural isomorphisms.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this verification: the four
axioms verified here are exactly Stacks Project, Derived Categories,
Definition 13.3.2 ([Tag 0145](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0145),
fetched and quoted: "the definition of a triangulated category as given in
Verdier's thesis", an additive category with an additive auto-equivalence
$[1]$ and a set of distinguished triangles subject to TR1--TR4, TR4 being
the octahedral axiom); the triangles and their morphisms are Definition
13.3.1 ([Tag 0144](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0144)) and the exact
functors of the last sentence are Definition 13.3.3 ([Tag
014V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014V)). The closest verification
of the axioms in Stacks for a category that is constructed rather than
assumed is Proposition 13.5.6 ([Tag
05R6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05R6)), which proves TR1--TR4 for
a localization $S^{-1}\mathcal D$ whose distinguished triangles are by
definition the images of distinguished triangles of $\mathcal D$, and Lemma
13.4.15 ([Tag 014C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014C)) is the
normal form for TR4. The blueprint adds the verification for the triangles
of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] together with the exactness of the
finite-stage inclusions $j_E$.

proof.text: Use the actual integral stages, their constant-section linear Hom groups and linear shifts from [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] and [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. Their inherited triangulation is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated], through the published integral full-subcategory instance. No new coefficient category or shift is chosen.

For each stage, compare its raw scalar localization with the existing rationalization at powers of the uniformizer. The tensorHomEquiv gives a fully faithful comparison and every rationalized object has an integral lattice, so this comparison is an equivalence. Its composite with the raw localization is naturally isomorphic to the rationalization functor, proving that the raw functor is a localization at the same morphism property. Apply Mathlib Triangulated.Localization.pretriangulated and isTriangulated directly for the already published shift. Its distinguished triangles are precisely the isomorphic integral images. The uniqueness assertion qbarStagePretriangulated_exists of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] identifies this pretriangulation with the published one. Transport the IsTriangulated proof along that equality; this proves qbarStageTriangulated without choosing a second shift.

For a finite field inclusion, the ambient derived tensor functor in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] is left adjoint to exact derived scalar restriction, with the mate shift comparison recorded in [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. Mathlib Adjunction.isTriangulated_leftAdjoint makes that tensor functor exact. Its integral restriction composes with the fully faithful target inclusion to give ambient tensor after source inclusion, and the integral shift was defined by this factorization. Functor.CommShift.ofComp_compatibility and Functor.isTriangulated_iff_comp_right therefore prove exactness of integral scalar extension. The preservation of the integral subcategory is precisely the existing pbcAmbientScalarExtension_preserves theorem, rather than a new hypothesis.

A distinguished rational source triangle is isomorphic to a localized integral distinguished triangle by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Apply exact integral tensor and then target localization. The latter preserves distinguishedness by the same integral-image characterization. The comparison pbcScalarIntegralComparison between localization followed by rational tensor and integral tensor followed by localization commutes with the published shifts by pbcScalarShift_exists in [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. Its mapTriangleIso, together with the two mapTriangleCompIso comparisons and the source triangle isomorphism, identifies the desired rational image triangle with the distinguished target image. Isomorphism closure proves qbarScalarExtensionExact, including repeated coefficient fields.

Retain the already proved generic inclusion and transition-identification checks. Additivity follows from pairPreadditive_exists and additivity of the identity transition. For shift compatibility of transIso, expand its identity representatives and the pair shift; pbcStageShift_coherence with the identity-stage inclusion cancels the final inverse shift comparison. These are qbarStageInclusionAdditive and qbarTransIsoCommShift.

Specialize the already stated commonStage_verdier_existsUnique theorem, attached to this node, to the actual pbcScalarSystem using the exact finite stages and transitions above. That generic theorem carries TR1--TR4 for exactly the CommonStageDistinguished predicate of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]: finite configurations are moved to a common stage, finite-stage cone, rotation, completion and octahedron axioms are applied, and the diagrams are mapped back with the coherent comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. The unique witness is exactly the one defining qbarPairPretriangulated. Project its IsTriangulated and exact-inclusion conjuncts, and use qbarTransIsoCommShift for the final conjunct of pbcVerdierAxioms. Thus the existing generic theorem supplies the blueprint axiom argument without a second invocation of the concrete distinguished-diagram-lifting or cone-independence theorems.

For TR1, (E,0) is zero and the identity triangle comes from stage E. The shift and distinguished triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]
satisfy the four Verdier axioms:

1. every morphism has a distinguished cone triangle, the identity triangle
   is distinguished, and distinguishedness is closed under isomorphism;
2. a triangle is distinguished if and only if its signed rotation is
   distinguished;
3. every commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
   triangles extends to a morphism of triangles;
4. cone triangles for composable maps can be placed in an octahedral diagram
   whose required faces commute and whose remaining cone triangle is
   distinguished.

Consequently $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated category. Every
finite-stage inclusion $j_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal P_T$ is exact, and
the identifications $j_FT_{F/E}\simeq j_E$ are exact natural isomorphisms.

proof.text:
TR1: every morphism has a cone triangle by
[def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]; the identity triangle is the cone
triangle of an identity (cone zero), and distinguishedness is closed under
isomorphism by the definition. TR2: by
[prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] a distinguished triangle and its
signed rotation may be represented over one common finite field, so the
finite-stage TR2 axiom makes the signed rotation distinguished (the shift in
the signed rotation being the $\sigma$-comparison of the definition). TR3:
given a commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
triangles, represent the two triangles over one common finite field (using
the transport isomorphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]) and apply the finite-stage TR3
axiom; the resulting vertical arrow transports back to $\mathcal P_T$. TR4:
the same common-stage representation of two composable morphisms, together
with the cone independence of [prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence], and the
finite-stage TR4 axiom produce the octahedral diagram whose remaining cone
triangle is distinguished. Hence $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated
category; $j_E$ is exact because cone triangles of $j_E(f)$ are the
corresponding common-stage cone triangles, and the identifications
$j_FT_{F/E}\simeq j_E$ are exact natural isomorphisms by
[prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence].
